questions.stem: In a circle with centre O, the angle at the centre (angle AOB) is 128 degrees. What is the angle at the circumference (angle ACB) subtended by the same arc?
questions.explanation: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference when both are subtended by the same arc. So angle ACB = 128 / 2 = 64 degrees.

questions.stem: AB is a diameter of a circle. Point C lies on the circumference. What is angle ACB?

options.text: It depends on where C is

questions.explanation: The angle in a semicircle is always 90 degrees. Any angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference is a right angle.

questions.stem: Two angles are subtended by the same arc at the circumference of a circle. One angle is 35 degrees. What is the other angle?
questions.explanation: Angles in the same segment are equal. Both angles are subtended by the same arc, so the other angle is also 35 degrees.

questions.stem: In a circle with centre O, angle ACB at the circumference is 54 degrees. What is angle AOB at the centre?
questions.explanation: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference. Angle AOB = 2 x 54 = 108 degrees.

questions.stem: A chord is drawn in a circle, creating two segments. Angle P in the major segment is 40 degrees (subtended by the chord). What is angle Q in the minor segment, subtended by the same chord?
questions.explanation: Angles in opposite segments are supplementary (they add up to 180 degrees). So angle Q = 180 - 40 = 140 degrees.
